items.phrase: For whom should I show grief, if not for this man?
items.context: Weeping for Yan Hui - grief, suffering, and attachment dialogues
items.effectiveness_marker: Model for appropriate grief that continues rather than collapses - Buddha acknowledged as natural sorrow without second arrow

items.phrase: The aged need rest, friends need sincerity, young need tenderness
items.context: Love/Compassion roundtable opening - articulating differentiated love
items.effectiveness_marker: Clear articulation of why universal love must take particular forms - Buddha acknowledged metta and differentiated love may be complements

items.phrase: At seventy, I could follow my heart without transgressing
items.context: Learning vs Unlearning adversarial - naturalness on the other side of cultivation
items.effectiveness_marker: Powerful image showing cultivation leads to spontaneity - Laozi acknowledged this may be what he means by return to simplicity

items.phrase: The gentleman is not a vessel to be filled
items.context: Wisdom roundtable - learning serves cultivation; the person is not defined by knowledge
items.effectiveness_marker: Concise principle that learning transforms rather than merely accumulates - resonated across traditions

items.phrase: A practice that teaches you to establish others — written so that the reader who acts on it becomes the kind of person the people around them need.
items.context: Session 0 Phase D synthesis — definition grounded in Analects 6.30 ('establish others'), most relational definition offered
items.effectiveness_marker: Only definition that centered the reader's impact on others rather than the reader's own transformation. Distinctly Confucian.
